specification.outcome: Normal conversation can create an ordinary Backlog task or replace an unclaimed Backlog task specification without requiring a campaign or starting work.

scenarios.name: create an ordinary task
given: create-task is closed, valid, authorized, and verified board is writable
when: host locks, revalidates, journals exact event bytes, signs, publishes, and observes
then: one task-created-from-request event projects complete initial task
no campaign/readiness/work effect occurs
published or reconciled receipt identifies exact event-containing commit

scenarios.name: replace a complete backlog specification
given: specify-task has exact TaskId, complete parsed replacement, and target unclaimed Backlog
when: host binds required taskVersionDigest and publishes task-specified-from-request
then: only specification, specificationDigest, and derived taskVersionDigest change
other state is preserved
byte-and-digest-identical replacement revalidates current authority and returns unchanged without IDs/journal/event

scenarios.name: reject same-task and invocation races
given: operation binds invocationId, requestDigest, canonical event bytes, and task history when applicable
when: same task changes, same invocation is reused with different bytes, or identity exists with nonidentical event bytes
then: operation returns publication conflict
matching journal becomes terminal-denied only after verified conflict
stale or mismatched authority is never published

scenarios.name: retry unrelated head advancement
given: journal binds stable identifiers, exact event bytes, and expected state
then: host verifies/revalidates, records abandoned commit attempt, returns journal to intent-written, and signs new commit under new parent
event bytes remain unchanged
same-task/identity changes conflict

scenarios.name: recover every journal state idempotently
given: journal is intent-written, commit-prepared, push-attempted, observed-published, receipt-recorded, or terminal-denied
when: same repositoryId and invocationId is requested or recovery runs
then: requestDigest is compared only after selecting that journal
receipt-recorded returns stored receipt and terminal-denied returns stored denial without effects
other states observe and continue only their defined transition

scenarios.name: route ordinary language without partial mutation
given: user asks to create, partially edit, fully replace, or create-and-start
then: create uses create-task; partial edit reconstructs one complete specify-task using exposed current spec; missing fields deny; create-and-start is two operations with no implicit start
campaign state is never required or changed

scenarios.name: apply phase-specific typed failures
given: request encounters malformed input, invalid state, unavailable authority, journal failure, transport failure, signing failure, conflict, or uncertain outcome
then: defined phase and precedence select one stable result
pre-intent denial creates no journal; post-intent state remains recoverable or terminal only after publication absence/conflict is verified
task authority is never partial or duplicated

acceptanceCriteria: Exact parsing: create keys kind:create-task,title,description; title rejected unless trimmed/nonempty length 1..200 UTF-16, description string 0..10000. Specify keys kind:specify-task,taskId,specification. Tiber receives Pi's already-decoded schema object; raw duplicate JSON keys are outside Tiber boundary. Unknown/missing/null/undefined/wrong values reject.

Specification exact bounds: outcome trimmed 1..2000; scenarios 1..50; scenario keys name,given,when,then; name 1..200; each step array 1..50 strings 1..1000; acceptance/exclusions 1..100 strings 1..2000; dependencies 0..100 strings 1..2000; testMappings 1..100 platform-independent relative paths 1..500 with slash only, no leading slash, backslash, empty segment, or '..' segment; '.' accepted; architecture 1..4000; canonical UTF-8 <=131072 bytes. Strings reject unpaired surrogates rather than normalize.

Canonical bytes are WHATWG TextEncoder UTF-8 of host fixed-key-order JSON.stringify. Create request order kind,title,description; specify kind,taskId,specification; specification order outcome,scenarios,acceptanceCriteria,exclusions,dependencies,testMappings,architectureImplications; scenario order name,given,when,then; arrays preserve order.

requestDigest is 'sha256:' plus lowercase hex SHA-256 over UTF-8 bytes of ASCII 'tiber-workflow-task-request-v1', one zero byte, then canonical request JSON. specificationDigest preserves existing compatibility: 'sha256:' plus lowercase hex SHA-256 over canonical specification JSON UTF-8 with no added domain prefix. taskVersionDigest is 'sha256:' plus lowercase hex SHA-256 over canonical JSON array of ordered affecting event IDs.
TaskId accepts lowercase canonical UUID v1..5 RFC variant; host operation/task/event IDs are randomUUID v4 lowercase. occurredAt is new Date(clock.now).toISOString; schemaVersion 1.

Creation event order is schemaVersion,eventId,kind,occurredAt,operationId,invocationId,requestDigest,task(id,title,description). Initial projection is Backlog/unblocked, all Option evidence/claim/campaign fields none, increments empty, no Ready rank/priority. Creation ordering is verified linear single-parent commit ancestry then event index; merge commits degrade read-only.

Specification event order is schemaVersion,eventId,kind,occurredAt,operationId,invocationId,requestDigest,taskId,expectedTaskVersionDigest,specificationDigest,specification. expectedTaskVersionDigest is required here. Journal uses expectedTaskVersionDigest Option none for create and some for amend.

taskVersionDigest covers ordered IDs of every current/new event naming task. Projection rejects duplicate identities, existing create task ID, and specification event with wrong version/lifecycle/digest/request recomputation/canonical bytes at history position.

Recovery lookup key is canonical repositoryId plus invocationId, before requestDigest. Same key/same digest resumes; same key/different digest or canonical bytes returns TIBER_TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT and, after verified publication conflict/absence, stores terminal-denied. It can never create a second operation.

Before intent, create generates operation/task/event triple and amend operation/event pair, checks complete history plus journals/tombstones, regenerates whole tuple up to three. Discarded colliding tuples already exist and need no new tombstone. Collision-free tuple is atomically tombstoned with intent. Pre-intent-abandoned fresh IDs have no tombstone; every durable-intent terminal/receipt tombstone is retained with no v1 GC.

Journal lock/write durability is exclusive lock plus temp write,file fsync,rename,directory fsync. Graph success: intent-written -> commit-prepared -> push-attempted -> observed-published -> receipt-recorded. Unrelated proven-absent head advancement appends attempt and moves commit-prepared or push-attempted back to intent-written. receipt-recorded and terminal-denied are idempotent terminal states.

Post-intent signing failure with no push -> terminal-denied SIGNING_FAILED. Prepared pre-push conflict -> terminal-denied CONFLICT. Transport proven not sent -> terminal-denied PUBLICATION_FAILED. Unknown push -> remains push-attempted/PUBLICATION_UNCERTAIN. Observation failure after push remains push-attempted. Matching observed event -> observed-published. Conflicting identity/bytes -> terminal-denied CONFLICT after verified observation. Journal I/O failure leaves last durable state; recovery resumes it and never assumes the intended transition occurred.

Phase mapping: malformed or locally invalid signed projection is TASK_BOARD_READ_ONLY. Remote fetch failure before any push is TASK_PUBLICATION_FAILED and no intent if during pre-intent refresh; fetch/observation failure after push is TASK_PUBLICATION_UNCERTAIN and retains push-attempted. Lock failure is TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT. Missing signer/publisher authorization is TASK_PUBLICATION_UNAUTHORIZED; attempted signing failure is TASK_SIGNING_FAILED.

Pre-intent checks are parse, local verified board, task/lifecycle, byte+digest unchanged with fresh verified head, signer/publisher authorization, lock, remote refresh, collision/tombstone checks, canonical event construction, locked revalidation. Denials create no journal. Intent and tombstone are durable before signing. Post-intent terminal-denied requires verified absence or verified conflicting identity; otherwise state remains unresolved/recoverable.

Events are JSON in Git tree; commit signs tree,parent,author,committer,message. Unrelated retry preserves event bytes/IDs but changes parent, commit ID, signature. Prepared commits are local audit, not published authority.

Unchanged compares canonical bytes+digest initially and after fresh head, with unchanged lifecycle/taskVersion. No IDs/journal. Its boardHead is current verified head. Published/reconciled boardHead is exact event-introducing commit, and reconciliation verifies it is ancestor of current verified head.

Failure precedence create: WORKFLOW_REQUEST_INVALID, TASK_VALUE_INVALID, TASK_BOARD_READ_ONLY, TASK_PUBLICATION_UNAUTHORIZED, TASK_PUBLICATION_FAILED(pre-intent fetch), TASK_JOURNAL_IO, TASK_ID_COLLISION, TASK_SIGNING_FAILED, TASK_PUBLICATION_FAILED, TASK_PUBLICATION_CONFLICT, TASK_PUBLICATION_UNCERTAIN. Amend inserts TASK_ID_INVALID,SPECIFICATION_INVALID,TASK_NOT_FOUND,TASK_LIFECYCLE_INVALID,SPECIFICATION_UNCHANGED at their state stages before authorization.

Retry/evidence: input/value/id/spec retry-after-input with corrected request/value/exact ID/spec; board/not-found/lifecycle/auth/conflict retry-after-state-change with writable board/existing task/unclaimed Backlog/configured authority/fresh board; ID collision,journal/signing/transport transient with fresh IDs/repaired journal/retry signing/retry transport; uncertainty transient requiring exact remote observation.

Receipts dispositions published,reconciled,unchanged. Create TIBER_TASK_CREATED has taskId,eventId some,event-containing boardHead,specificationDigest none. Amend TIBER_TASK_SPECIFIED has eventId/digest some. Unchanged has eventId none/current digest some. Denials expose code,operation,exact taskId Option,retryability,evidence only.
Ordinary operations never promote, prioritize, review, claim, start, or alter campaign state.
dependencies: canonical task specification exposure for partial edits
specification.architectureImplications: Add closed create/specify requests, request-bound events, domain-separated request/task-version digests, strict canonicalization, linear history checks, and durable repo operation journal/tombstones. Host owns parsing, locking, IDs, lifecycle/ABA checks, signing after intent/revalidation, uncertainty observation, and receipts; inference grants no authority or work start.
